passages.text: When Jesus saw the crowds, He went up on the mountain and sat down. His disciples came to Him, and He began to teach them, saying: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the crowds.
He went up on the mountain.
He sat down.
His disciples came to Him.
Jesus opened His mouth.
He taught them.
He said, “Blessed are the poor in spirit.
The kingdom of heaven belongs to them.”
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος καὶ καθίσαντος αὐτοῦ προσῆλθαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς λέγων Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι Ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν

passages.text: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He taught them on the mountain.
He said, “Blessed are those who mourn.
God will comfort them.”
passages.original: Μακάριοι οἱ πενθοῦντες Ὅτι αὐτοὶ παρακληθήσονται

passages.text: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples on the mountain.
He taught them about God's blessings.
He said, "Blessed are the meek."
Meek people are gentle and humble.
God will give the earth to the meek.
The meek will inherit the earth.
passages.original: Μακάριοι οἱ πραεῖς Ὅτι αὐτοὶ κληρονομήσουσιν τὴν γῆν

passages.text: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He described people who desire righteousness.
These people hunger for righteousness.
They thirst for righteousness.
God calls these people blessed.
God will fill them.
God will satisfy their desire for righteousness.
passages.original: Μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες καὶ διψῶντες τὴν δικαιοσύνην Ὅτι αὐτοὶ χορτασθήσονται

passages.text: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
passages.sermon:
The merciful are blessed.
Merciful people show kindness and compassion.
God will show mercy to the merciful.
God will give mercy to those who give mercy.
passages.original: Μακάριοι οἱ ἐλεήμονες Ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἐλεηθήσονται

passages.text: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He described people who are pure in heart.
A pure heart means a heart that is clean and sincere.
These people do not have evil or deceit in their hearts.
God blesses the pure in heart.
God promises that the pure in heart will see Him.
passages.original: Μακάριοι οἱ καθαροὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ Ὅτι αὐτοὶ τὸν Θεὸν ὄψονται

passages.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.
passages.sermon: Peacemakers act to bring peace.\r\nGod will call peacemakers His sons.
passages.original: Μακάριοι οἱ εἰρηνοποιοί Ὅτι αὐτοὶ υἱοὶ Θεοῦ κληθήσονται

passages.text: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He described people who are blessed.
Some people suffer because they do what is right.
These people are persecuted for righteousness.
God calls these people blessed.
The kingdom of heaven belongs to them.
passages.original: Μακάριοι οἱ δεδιωγμένοι ἕνεκεν δικαιοσύνης Ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν

passages.text: Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His followers.
He says, “You are blessed when people insult you because of Me.
You are blessed when people persecute you because of Me.
You are blessed when people tell lies about you and say all kinds of evil things against you because of Me.”
passages.original: Μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν ὀνειδίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ διώξωσιν καὶ εἴπωσιν πᾶν πονηρὸν καθ’ ὑμῶν ψευδόμενοι ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ

passages.text: Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven; for in the same way they persecuted the prophets before you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His followers.
He told them to rejoice.
He told them to be glad.
He said their reward is great in heaven.
He explained that people persecuted the prophets before them in the same way.
passages.original: χαίρετε καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε ὅτι ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς οὕτως γὰρ ἐδίωξαν τοὺς προφήτας τοὺς πρὸ ὑμῶν

passages.text: You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its savor, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by men.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His followers.
He said, "You are the salt of the earth."
Salt has a special purpose.
Salt gives flavor and preserves food.
If salt loses its taste, it cannot become salty again.
Salt without taste is useless.
People throw it away.
People walk on it.
Salt must keep its purpose to be useful.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ ἅλας τῆς γῆς ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ ἐν τίνι ἁλισθήσεται εἰς οὐδὲν ἰσχύει ἔτι εἰ μὴ βληθὲν ἔξω καταπατεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He said, "You are the light of the world."
Light shines and shows the way.
A city stands on a hill.
People cannot hide a city on a hill.
Everyone can see it.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου οὐ δύναται πόλις κρυβῆναι ἐπάνω ὄρους κειμένη

passages.text: Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a basket. Instead, they set it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.
passages.sermon: People do not light a lamp and put it under a basket.\r\nPeople put a lamp on a stand.\r\nThe lamp gives light to everyone in the house.
passages.original: οὐδὲ καίουσιν λύχνον καὶ τιθέασιν αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν καὶ λάμπει πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ

passages.text: In the same way, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He said, "You are the light of the world."
Let your light shine in front of people.
Let people see your good deeds.
Then people will praise your Father in heaven.
passages.original: οὕτως λαμψάτω τὸ φῶς ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὅπως ἴδωσιν ὑμῶν τὰ καλὰ ἔργα καὶ δοξάσωσιν τὸν πατέρα ὑμῶν τὸν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
Jesus says, “Do not think I came to destroy the Law or the Prophets.
I did not come to destroy them.
I came to fulfill them.”
passages.original: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἢ τοὺς προφήτας οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι

passages.text: For I tell you truly, until heaven and earth pass away, not a single jot, not a stroke of a pen, will disappear from the Law until everything is accomplished.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus says this truth with certainty.
He says, “I tell you truly.”
He says, “Heaven and earth will remain.”
He says, “Until heaven and earth pass away, the Law will remain.”
He says, “Not even the smallest letter will disappear from the Law.”
He says, “Not even the smallest mark will disappear from the Law.”
He says, “This will continue until everything is accomplished.”
passages.original: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ἕως ἂν παρέλθῃ ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται

passages.text: So then, whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do likewise will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever practices and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples about the commandments of God.
He said that the commandments are important in the kingdom of heaven.
If a person breaks even one of the least of these commandments, that person does wrong.
If that person also teaches others to break the commandments, that person does even more wrong.
God will call that person least in the kingdom of heaven.
If a person obeys the commandments, that person does right.
If that person also teaches others to obey the commandments, that person does even more right.
God will call that person great in the kingdom of heaven.
passages.original: Ὃς ἐὰν οὖν λύσῃ μίαν τῶν ἐντολῶν τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων καὶ διδάξῃ οὕτως τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐλάχιστος κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὃς δ’ ἂν ποιήσῃ καὶ διδάξῃ οὗτος μέγας κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν

passages.text: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said this truth clearly.
You must have righteousness.
Your righteousness must be greater than the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees.
If your righteousness is not greater, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
passages.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ περισσεύσῃ ὑμῶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη πλεῖον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν

passages.text: You have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not murder’ and ‘Anyone who murders will be subject to judgment.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He reminded them of a command given long ago.
God gave this command to their ancestors.
The command says, “Do not murder.”
Anyone who murders will face judgment.
passages.original: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις Οὐ φονεύσεις ὃς δ’ ἂν φονεύσῃ ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει

passages.text: But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment. Again, anyone who says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be subject to the Sanhedrin. But anyone who says, ‘You fool!’ will be subject to the fire of hell.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
Jesus teaches about righteousness.
Jesus says, “Anyone who is angry with his brother will face judgment.”
Anyone who says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will answer to the council.”
Anyone who says, ‘You fool!’ will face the fire of hell.”
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὀργιζόμενος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ Ῥακά ἔνοχος ἔσται τῷ συνεδρίῳ ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ Μωρέ ἔνοχος ἔσται εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός

passages.text: So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar. First go and be reconciled to your brother; then come and offer your gift.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He teaches about offering gifts to God.
If you bring your gift to the altar, you want to worship God.
You remember that your brother has something against you.
Leave your gift there in front of the altar.
Go first and make peace with your brother.
After you are reconciled, come back.
Then offer your gift to God.
passages.original: Ἐὰν οὖν προσφέρῃς τὸ δῶρόν σου ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον κἀκεῖ μνησθῇς ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἔχει τι κατὰ σοῦ ἄφες ἐκεῖ τὸ δῶρόν σου ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ ὕπαγε πρῶτον διαλλάγηθι τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου καὶ τότε ἐλθὼν πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρόν σου

passages.text: Reconcile quickly with your adversary, while you are still on the way to court. Otherwise, he may hand you over to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and you may be thrown into prison.
passages.sermon:
Jesus teaches his disciples about reconciliation.
He says, “Make peace quickly with your adversary.
Do this while you are still with him on the way to court.
If you do not make peace, your adversary may hand you over to the judge.
The judge may then hand you over to the officer.
The officer may throw you into prison.”
passages.original: ἴσθι εὐνοῶν τῷ ἀντιδίκῳ σου ταχὺ ἕως ὅτου εἶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ μή‿ ποτέ σε παραδῷ ὁ ἀντίδικος τῷ κριτῇ καὶ ὁ κριτὴς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν βληθήσῃ

passages.text: Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to his listeners.
Jesus says something true and important.
Jesus says, “You will not get out from there until you have paid the last penny.”
You must pay everything you owe before you are released.
passages.original: ἀμὴν λέγω σοι οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως ἂν ἀποδῷς τὸν ἔσχατον κοδράντην

passages.text: You have heard that it was said, ‘Do not commit adultery.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He taught them about God’s law.
He said, “You have heard this command.”
The command says, “Do not commit adultery.”
passages.original: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη Οὐ μοιχεύσεις

passages.text: But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
Jesus teaches about adultery.
Jesus says this truth clearly.
Anyone who looks at a woman with lust has already sinned.
He has committed adultery with her in his heart.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ βλέπων γυναῖκα πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτὴν ἤδη ἐμοίχευσεν αὐτὴν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: If your right eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He warns them about sin.
If your right eye causes you to sin, remove it.
Throw it away from you.
It is better to lose one part of your body.
It is better than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὁ δεξιὸς σκανδαλίζει σε ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου βληθῇ εἰς γέενναν

passages.text: And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to depart into hell.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He warns them about sin.
If your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off.
Throw it away from you.
It is better for you to lose one part of your body.
It is better than for your whole body to go into hell.
passages.original: καὶ εἰ ἡ δεξιά σου χεὶρ σκανδαλίζει σε ἔκκοψον αὐτὴν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου εἰς γέενναν ἀπέλθῃ

passages.text: It has also been said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’
passages.sermon:
Moses gave a command to the people of Israel.
He said, “Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.”
This certificate is a written document.
The husband must give this document to his wife if he sends her away.
This rule is about divorce.
It tells the husband to make the separation official with a certificate.
passages.original: Ἐρρέθη δέ Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ δότω αὐτῇ ἀποστάσιον

passages.text: But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, brings adultery upon her. And he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
Jesus teaches about divorce.
Anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, causes her to commit adultery.
Anyone who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι καὶ ὃς ἐὰν ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσῃ μοιχᾶται

passages.text: Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill your vows to the Lord.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He referred to the teachings given to their ancestors.
He said, "You have heard this command before."
The command is, "Do not break your oath."
The command also says, "Keep the vows you make to the Lord."
God expects you to keep your promises to Him.
God wants you to be faithful to your word.
passages.original: Πάλιν ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις Οὐκ ἐπιορκήσεις ἀποδώσεις δὲ τῷ Κυρίῳ τοὺς ὅρκους σου

passages.text: But I tell you not to swear at all: either by heaven, for it is God’s throne; or by the earth, for it is His footstool; or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
Jesus says, "Do not swear at all."
Do not swear by heaven.
Heaven is God's throne.
Do not swear by the earth.
The earth is God's footstool.
Do not swear by Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is the city of the great King.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ὀμόσαι ὅλως μήτε ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὅτι θρόνος ἐστὶν τοῦ Θεοῦ μήτε ἐν τῇ γῇ ὅτι ὑποπόδιόν ἐστιν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ μήτε εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ὅτι πόλις ἐστὶν τοῦ μεγάλου Βασιλέως

passages.text: Nor should you swear by your head, for you cannot make a single hair white or black.
passages.sermon:
Do not swear by your own head.
You cannot make a single hair white.
You cannot make a single hair black.
You do not have this power.
passages.original: μήτε ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ σου ὀμόσῃς ὅτι οὐ δύνασαι μίαν τρίχα λευκὴν ποιῆσαι ἢ μέλαιναν

passages.text: Simply let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’ Anything more comes from the evil one.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He teaches them about honesty.
He says, “Let your word be simple.”
Say ‘Yes’ if you mean yes.
Say ‘No’ if you mean no.
Do not add anything extra to your answer.
If you say more than this, it comes from the evil one.
passages.original: ἔστω δὲ ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν Ναὶ ναί οὒ Οὔ τὸ δὲ περισσὸν τούτων ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἐστιν

passages.text: You have heard that it was said, ‘Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He taught them about the law.
He said, “You have heard this before.”
The law said, ‘Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.’
This means people expected equal payback for harm.
This was a rule for justice in the past.
People believed in returning harm for harm.
Jesus reminded them of this teaching.
passages.original: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη Ὀφθαλμὸν ἀντὶ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ ὀδόντα ἀντὶ ὀδόντος

passages.text: But I tell you not to resist an evil person. If someone slaps you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also; if someone wants to sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well; and if someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
Jesus teaches about how to respond to evil people.
Jesus says, do not resist an evil person.
If someone hits you on your right cheek, offer him your other cheek also.
If someone wants to sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well.
If someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ἀντιστῆναι τῷ πονηρῷ ἀλλ’ ὅστις σε ῥαπίζει εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν σιαγόνα σου στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν ὕπαγε μετ’ αὐτοῦ δύο

passages.text: Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.
passages.sermon: Jesus teaches his followers to show generosity.\r\nGive to anyone who asks you for something.\r\nDo not turn away from anyone who wants to borrow from you.
passages.original: τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δός καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς

passages.text: You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor’ and ‘Hate your enemy.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He referred to a teaching they knew.
He said, “You have heard this before.”
The teaching says, “Love your neighbor.”
The teaching also says, “Hate your enemy.”
passages.original: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου καὶ μισήσεις τὸν ἐχθρόν σου

passages.text: But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, that you may be sons of your Father in heaven. He causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His followers.
Jesus commands them to love their enemies.
Jesus tells them to pray for those who persecute them.
God is their Father in heaven.
Jesus wants them to become children of their Father in heaven.
God makes His sun rise on evil people and good people.
God sends rain on righteous people and unrighteous people.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν διωκόντων ὑμᾶς ὅπως γένησθε υἱοὶ τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὅτι τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλει ἐπὶ πονηροὺς καὶ ἀγαθοὺς καὶ βρέχει ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ἀδίκους

passages.text: If you love those who love you, what reward will you get? Do not even tax collectors do the same?
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
He teaches about love.
He says, “If you love only those who love you, you will not receive a reward from God.”
Even tax collectors love those who love them.
You do nothing special if you love only those who love you.
passages.original: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀγαπήσητε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς τίνα μισθὸν ἔχετε οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ τελῶναι τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν

passages.text: And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing more than others? Do not even Gentiles do the same?
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
He teaches about love and kindness.
If you greet only your brothers, you do nothing special.
Gentiles also greet only their own people.
You do not do more than others if you greet only your brothers.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἀσπάσησθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὑμῶν μόνον τί περισσὸν ποιεῖτε οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ ἐθνικοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν

passages.text: Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
passages.sermon: God is your Father in heaven.\r\nGod is perfect.\r\nYou must also be perfect, just as your heavenly Father is perfect.
passages.original: Ἔσεσθε οὖν ὑμεῖς τέλειοι ὡς ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τέλειός ἐστιν
